children: Homeowners insurance provider Orion180 Insurance Group plans to sell 20 million shares at between $15 and $17 apiece in its initial public offering.

At the $16 midpoint of that price range, the Melbourne, Fla., company said it expects net proceeds of about $296 million, or roughly $341 million if the underwriters exercise an option to buy an additional three million shares.

Orion180 said it would have about 102 million shares outstanding after the IPO, assuming an exercise of the overallotment option, for a market capitalization of about $1.63 billion at the $16-a-share pricing midpoint.
Orion180 said it has applied to list its shares on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol OIG.
